neighbours.label: Gospel narratives of Jesus confronting his opponents: the religious leaders, scribes and Sadducees who challenge him
fire: In the temple courts the religious leaders questioned Jesus about his authority.
Jesus warned the crowd about the scribes, who devour widows' houses.
Once again the Pharisees tried to trap Jesus with a question about taxes.
He silenced the Sadducees with his answer about the resurrection.
On Friday morning the chief priests brought Jesus before Pilate.
The teachers of the law grew angry because Jesus healed on the Sabbath.
As the elders plotted against him, Jesus kept teaching in the temple.
Jesus rebuked the Pharisees for honouring God with their lips alone.
quiet: In the temple courts the children sang and praised God with joy.
Jesus told the crowd about the widow who gave two small coins.
Once again the disciples asked Jesus to explain a parable about seeds.
He comforted the sisters of Lazarus with his words about life.
On Sunday morning the women found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
The fishermen were amazed because Jesus filled their nets with fish.
As the sun set over the lake, Jesus kept teaching from the boat.
Jesus blessed the little children and laid his hands on them.
